answer: A compute-bonded identity registry resists sybils. To join, an agent must forge a credential by solving a verifiable delay puzzle bound to its public key; the registry admits a node only when the proof lands on-chain. Ten thousand sock puppets cost ten thousand sequential proof-hours, since nothing amortizes across key-specific proofs. Honest operators pay once and keep signing, so the registry is an oasis of cheap participation while a sybil farm burns irrecoverable capital. A bridge between registries carries one attestation across markets, so reputation earned once keeps working.
